name: Question 3
problem:
Which of the following could be the graph of a function $f(x)$ that satisfies the conditions below?

- ${f}^{′}(2)=0$

- if $x\in (-\infty ,2)$ then ${f}^{′}(x)<0$

- if $x\in (2,\infty )$ then ${f}^{″}(x)<0$
worked_solution:
We summarize all the given information in the following table:

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,2)$ | $2$ | $(2,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $-$ | $0$ |  |
| ${f}^{″}$ |  |  | $-$ |
| $f$ |  |  |  |

This gives us the following information about the graph of $f:$

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,2)$ | $2$ | $(2,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $-$ | $0$ |  |
| ${f}^{″}$ |  |  | $-$ |
| $f$ | $↘$ | Zero slope | $⌢$ |

So, we can conclude that

- the graph of $y=f(x)$ has a zero slope when $x=2,$

- $f(x)$ is decreasing on $(-\infty ,2),$ and

- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(2,\infty ).$
